name: Wilmington, Ohio, 29 June 2012 (afternoon balloon)
line: Extremely unstable, very moist air (CAPE about 6300 J/kg) with moderate wind shear (19 m/s over 6 km).
note: The balloon launched at 1800 UTC (2 pm local time). A 200 x 120 km area for 3 hours; the ends of the line feel the open sides. The storm is started by a gentle push of rising air, as CM1's updraft nudging does. In a 1 km run the push starts one storm, not a line, and it has rained itself out within about 45 minutes (measured). This day's sounding in an idealized storm, not a reconstruction of that day's storms. The area is not made smaller than 120 km, because CM1's parcel grid covers 120 km; the fit makes the grid coarser or the storm shorter instead.
